description.en: To verify Kirchhoff’s Current Law by measuring that the total current entering the junction is equal to the total current leaving it in a resistive DC circuit.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
To use this feature, click on the “AI Guide” button. The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.

The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct. 

Note: If a wire is connected incorrectly, click the corresponding label number to remove the connection.
The AUTO CONNECT button makes all the connections automatically.
The ADD button adds the readings to the observation table.
The PLOT button will display the graph of the recorded readings.
The RESET button refresh the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.

Set the values of R1, R2, and R3 by moving the resistance sliders. These resistance values will remain constant throughout the experiment to ensure accurate verification of Kirchhoff’s Current Law. 

 **Range:** 1 - 5 kΩ

This section provides the required DC voltage to the circuit. The display shows the active voltage supplied to the circuit, and the slider can be used to set the desired voltage value. 

 **Rating:** 15 V DC

Ammeters are used to measure the branch currents in the circuit. Record the current readings for each branch at different voltage values. The measured currents will be used to compare the current entering and leaving the junction for KCL verification. 

 **Rating:** 0 - 10 mA
This section displays the circuit and allows users to make the required connections by dragging and dropping wires between the connection points.

This table will record the measured branch currents I<sub>1</sub>, I<sub>2</sub>, and I<sub>3</sub> at different voltages.  These readings will be used later to plot the graph and verify Kirchhoff’s Current Law.
This section displays the equations used to determine an equivalent resistance and the branch currents.

In this section, the recorded reading will be selected for theoretical verification, and the required resistance and current values will be calculated to verify KCL. In addition, after recording the observations, a current v/s voltage graph will be displayed using the measured readings for analysis.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table, graph and theoretical verification, generate the report. The report will include the time taken to complete the simulation, key parameters, recorded readings, graph, user-calculated results and conclusion.
